cap: The twisted pedicle fails in order of wall strength. Thin-walled, low-pressure veins and lymphatics collapse first, while the thick-walled artery still delivers blood, so the ovary swells with venous congestion and edema. Rising tissue pressure then stops arterial inflow and the ovary infarcts. Doppler flow can persist early, so a normal study does not exclude torsion, and a heavy ovary with sudden one-sided pain needs prompt surgery.
